verdict.rationale: Maritime documents some natural-language control of its own. You can tell an OpenClaw or Hermes agent "send me a digest every weekday at 9" and the platform turns that into real wake triggers (maritime-docs-32, maritime-docs-48). Your Maritime agent can also run migrations from a provider runbook (maritime-docs-16). Broader natural-language operation, such as installing, authenticating and deploying, relies on an external assistant like Claude or Cursor driving the agent-friendly CLI from a single pasted prompt (maritime-docs-42, maritime-docs-22). Missing for 10: a first-party natural-language interface covering general platform management (deploy, configure, keys, billing), natural-language trigger control beyond specific template families, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
